add.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria (Wikipedia) - Shari'a-state penalty context for Kebbi
add.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Nigeria' (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/815928c9a45eeba4.txt) situates Kebbi inside the northern Shari'a block: in Shari'a-governed northern states punishments for same-sex acts range from imprisonment to capital punishment, and lesbianism is punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death penalties applied only in Kano and Katsina - i.e., Kebbi sits on the lashing/imprisonment tier rather than the capital tier, consistent with the record's own statute reading. It also documents the cross-dressing layer (prison or fine for men who dress or behave as women; Kano 2025 one-year imprisonment sentence). Placement axis: nothing on where trans prisoners are housed - no housing, segregation or placement rule for Kebbi or Nigeria anywhere in the article.

add.title: LGBTQ people in Nigeria (Wikipedia) - criminalisation and trans visibility
add.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched in full via MediaWiki API, cached research/fetched/767cdbb3294908bd.txt) covering the community-facing picture: the Criminal Code criminalises sex acts between men with penalties up to 14 years' imprisonment, gross indecency between men up to 3 years, lesbianism punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death in Kano and Katsina, and cross-dressing penalised in some states (Kano up to one year in prison or a fine for men who dress or behave as women; 2025 Kano sentence of a TikToker to one year in prison). The article cites trans-specific coverage ('I feel invisible': The challenges of being trans in Nigeria, Timinepre Cole) but contains no trans-prisoner housing or placement information for Kebbi or Nigeria.
